sections.html:
Casey County covers about 446 square miles with one city, Liberty, and the 2020 census classed the whole population as rural. The count was 15,941 people in 6,270 households and 7,366 housing units, and 14.9 percent of those units stood empty. About 76 percent of occupied homes are lived in by their owners, which means a typical sale here is someone leaving their own home.

Most parcels are farm tracts, hill lots in the Knobs or houses along the state routes. Hillside access, wells, septic systems and road frontage are worth documenting before you list. Only homes inside Liberty raise city tax questions. For everyone else, the assessed value is the first number to examine.

sections.h2: Which office handles which tax question
sections.html:
The year runs on the standard Kentucky cycle: value fixed by the PVA as of January 1, collection by the sheriff from early October to April 15, and leftovers passed to the county clerk. Ask the PVA about value, the sheriff about this year's amount, and the clerk about anything delinquent.

Casey County offices for property tax questions
OfficeWherePhoneHandles
Property Valuation Administrator133 Courthouse Square, Liberty (mail: P O Box 38)606-787-7621Assessments, homestead applications, appeal conferences
County Clerk625 Campbellsville Street, Liberty (mail: P.O. Box 310)606-787-6471Delinquent tax bills, the annual tax sale, lien releases

The clerk keeps weekday hours of 8:00 am to 4:30 pm, except holidays. For the sheriff's address and number, the clerk or the PVA can point you the right way.

Your sheriff's bill sets the base amount, and the payment date adjusts it. KRS 134.015 gives 2 percent off for paying everything by November 1, charges face value through the end of December, tacks on 5 percent for January, and moves to a 10 percent penalty on February 1 plus the sheriff's add-on fee.

Unpaid tax clings to the parcel as a lien for eleven years, no matter who owns it. If collection starts late in a given year, the Department of Revenue can substitute a schedule that gives owners 30 days at each stage.

If you've lost your bill, get the parcel number from the PVA or clerk and ask the sheriff for a copy. Mortgage escrow doesn't take the bill out of your name, so confirm the payment posted before closing.

sections.h2: How to contest a Casey County valuation
sections.html:
Request a conference with the PVA during the public viewing of the tax roll. That period lasts thirteen days from the first Monday of May, and you can ask to do the conference by phone.

If that fails, mail or deliver a written petition to the county clerk by the workday after viewing ends. Include the parcel, your reasons and your opinion of fair cash value. A hearing follows about a month later. Evidence carries the day: sales of similar houses, construction cost records, an insurance policy or a recent appraisal. Under KRS 133.120 the board denies an appeal when the owner won't supply reasonable value information on request.

  • Hold the PVA conference first, because skipping it closes later doors.
  • Keep paying on the value you claimed while the case is pending.
  • A raised value brings a supplemental bill, due the day it is prepared.

After April 15 an unpaid bill goes to the clerk and can be sold to a private buyer at an annual summer sale. The clerk receives the sheriff's list in April, runs a notice in The Casey County News in July, and holds the sale in August at 9:00 am in its office on Campbellsville Street. Call 606-787-6471 for the current year's dates.

Owners can pay up to the moment the sale opens. Bidders register with the clerk ten days ahead and pay a recording fee of $46 per lien assignment. A buyer who wants more than three certificates in the county, or more than five statewide, must also register with the Department of Revenue.

The sale runs like a draft. Registered buyers draw numbers at random, then take turns picking certificates from the lists they filed, sometimes one certificate per round when the volume is high. The clerk's office tells buyers it won't research bills for them, so a parcel with a problem, such as a bankruptcy filing, is the buyer's risk. Once someone buys your certificate, you owe that buyer and fees can grow. Paying earlier prevents it.

If you already know a bill is going to the clerk, ask whether a payment arrangement is possible and whether the clerk will take a partial payment. Get any agreement in writing, and make sure it covers the fees the certificate has picked up.

Kentucky's homestead exemption covers owners in their retirement years or with a total disability. A fixed dollar amount comes off the home's assessed value. The Department of Revenue set it at $49,100 for 2025 and 2026 and publishes a new amount every second year. File with the Casey County PVA and bring proof such as a driver's license or passport.

Only the resident owner gets it. Moving into care or selling mid-year? Let the PVA know so the next bill is right.

sections.h2: Closing a sale when tax is unpaid
sections.html:
Collect written balances from both the clerk and the sheriff for your closing agent. Whatever is still owed at the table is deducted from your price, and a lien the clerk filed has to be released before the buyer takes clean title. Releases are recorded at the clerk's office for a posted fee.

For an inherited, empty or worn-down house, a cash buyer that takes the property as is can pay the tax from the price. That keeps your parcel off the August list, where delinquent bills become public.

Work through it in this order. Call the PVA to confirm the parcel and the exemption on file. Ask the sheriff for the current balance. Ask the clerk whether any earlier bill was certified and what the release will cost. Then bring the figures to your closing agent before you sign a contract, so the buyer's offer is based on the real payoff.

Expect the lien release to take a little time to record, so ask the clerk how long it runs. Selling before the next penalty date keeps the amount from rising while you wait. If the property is farmland or hill acreage, confirm the acreage on the PVA's map matches your deed, since the bill follows the PVA record and not your memory of the boundaries.

faqs.q: Where do I find my Casey County property tax bill?
faqs.a: Ask the Casey County sheriff's office, which sends the bills. If you lack its number, the clerk at 606-787-6471 or the PVA at 606-787-7621 can point you to it and help identify your parcel.

faqs.q: When is the Casey County tax sale?
faqs.a: The clerk holds it each August at 9:00 am at 625 Campbellsville Street in Liberty. Owners can pay their unpaid bills up to the start of the sale.

faqs.q: How big is the homestead exemption for Casey County owners?
faqs.a: The state figure is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, subtracted from the assessed value. It is open to owners 65 and up or totally disabled, and you apply through the Casey County PVA.

faqs.q: Is it too late to appeal if I missed the May viewing period?
faqs.a: Usually yes. The PVA conference and the clerk filing both fall inside that window, unless the state approved an extension of up to 25 days. Ask the PVA whether one applied.

faqs.q: Does unpaid tax stop me from selling Casey County land?
faqs.a: No. The bill and any lien get cleared at closing from your proceeds. Ask the sheriff or clerk for payoff amounts first so the title company can deduct them.
